messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The current bug report explains that the TAR checksum verification fails when the checksum field in the TAR header uses zero padding aligned to the left instead of the expected NULL-SPACE terminator on the right. This causes loss of the last two digits of the checksum, making the checksum validation fail for otherwise valid TAR files.

The key point lies in the method `TarUtils.verifyCheckSum(byte[] header)` which is responsible for checksum verification of the TAR header. This method iterates over the header bytes and specifically processes the bytes in the checksum field (starting at offset 148, length 8 bytes). The code allows for reading up to the first 6 digits of an octal number representing the stored checksum. If a byte within the checksum field is between '0' and '7' and fewer than 6 digits have been read, it adds the digit to the `storedSum`. Otherwise, if at least one digit has been processed, it stops processing digits after 6.

In addition, this method replaces each byte in the checksum field with a space character (0x20) when summing the unsigned and signed sums of the rest of the header bytes, as per TAR specification.

The restrictive acceptance of only the first 6 octal digits (and ignoring other padding characters or the exact alignment of the checksum field) causes the method to fail when the checksum is left zero-padded instead of right NULL-SPACE terminated. This behavior in `verifyCheckSum` does not accommodate alternative valid TAR checksum formats, especially those with leading zeros for padding, causing the stored checksum calculation to be incorrect (last 2 digits lost) and, thus, failing the validation.

The failing test `testCOMPRESS335` loads a TAR file "COMPRESS-335.tar" presumably containing this alternate checksum format (left zero padded). Since the checksum verification in `TarUtils.verifyCheckSum` fails this TAR file, the test also fails.

Recent reports mentioning valid TAR files being falsely rejected or recognized incorrectly also indirectly support that the checksum verification logic is overly strict or incorrectly handles certain edge cases in TAR headers.

In summary, the bug arises because `TarUtils.verifyCheckSum` method enforces strict parsing of only the first 6 octal digits of the 8-byte checksum field and does not correctly handle zero padding on the left side, causing the stored checksum to be miscalculated and checksum verification to fail for otherwise valid archives.

The fix would involve relaxing or correcting the parsing logic in `verifyCheckSum` to properly handle TAR checksum fields with leading zeros or different padding approaches.

---

Which methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarUtils.verifyCheckSum(byte[])
